title: In 897, a Pope Dug Up a Dead Pope and Put the Corpse on Trial

scenes.text: A pope once put a corpse on trial.
Rome, the year 897. Pope Stephen the Sixth had his predecessor, Formosus, dug up, nine months after his death.
The body was dressed in papal robes and propped up on the papal throne, to face the charges.
Stephen declared Formosus's papacy invalid, and every act of it void, including the priests he had ordained.
Then the corpse was dragged through the streets of Rome and dumped in the Tiber.
Within months an uprising removed Stephen. He was imprisoned and strangled. The dead pope's judge was dead by the end of the year.

description:
In 897, Pope Stephen VI had the nine-month-old corpse of his predecessor Formosus exhumed, dressed in papal vestments and propped on the papal throne to be tried.
Stephen annulled Formosus's pontificate and voided his acts, including the holy orders he had conferred, then had the body dragged through the streets and thrown into the Tiber. Months later an insurrection removed Stephen; he was imprisoned and strangled.
What is the strangest trial in history you know of?
